title: Claude Code's 2026 Feature Wave: Auto Mode, Agent View, Artifacts, and More
content:
## Overview

Since the [Claude Code Overview](claude-code-overview) page was written, Claude Code shipped a dense sequence of features through 2026 that meaningfully changed how sessions run day to day — most notably a shift from permission-prompt-driven execution toward supervised autonomy, and from single-session CLI use toward a fleet of concurrent, observable agents. This page tracks the major additions; see the weekly digest at `code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new` for the full detailed changelog.

---

## Auto Mode

**Auto mode**, first shipped in research preview (Week 13, March 2026), replaces manual permission prompts with a classifier that decides in the background whether an action is safe to run automatically or should be blocked outright. It sits between "approve everything" and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: safe reads and edits proceed without interruption, while destructive or ambiguous actions (like transcript tampering or `rm -rf` on unresolved variables) are blocked rather than merely flagged.

Auto mode rolled out progressively across account tiers and providers through mid-2026: Pro plan support (Week 21), then Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry (Week 23), reaching general availability on those three providers without an opt-in flag by Week 29 (mid-July 2026).

---

## Agent View and Background Subagents

`claude agents` opened as a single screen showing every running Claude Code session — what's active, what's blocked waiting on you, and what's finished — with each row showing a colored state word and a classifier-written headline (Week 28).

As of Week 27 (late June 2026), **subagents run in the background by default**, so the main session keeps working while a subagent executes rather than blocking on it. Background subagents can now spawn their own sub-agents, with chains capped at five levels deep, and their permission prompts surface in the main session instead of auto-denying.

---

## Artifacts Go Live

Artifacts — publishing a session's output as a shareable page on claude.ai — reached beta on Team and Enterprise in Week 25 (mid-June 2026) with the ability to update in place as a session works. By Week 29, published artifacts can call a viewer's own **MCP connectors** each time they open the page, so a dashboard-style artifact can show live data or take actions on demand rather than a frozen snapshot from when it was built. That same week added public sharing links, editor roles for Team/Enterprise, and artifact creation from Claude Tag (Slack) sessions.

---

## Computer Use, Ultrareview, and Ultraplan

- **Computer use in the CLI** (research preview, Week 14, late March 2026): Claude can open native applications, click through a UI, and verify a change from the terminal — useful for closing the loop on anything only a GUI can confirm.
- **`/ultrareview`** (public preview, Week 17, April 2026; `claude ultrareview` for CI, Week 18): a fleet of bug-hunting agents runs in the cloud and reports findings back to the CLI or Desktop automatically.
- **Ultraplan** (early preview, Week 15, April 2026): draft a plan in the cloud from the CLI, review and comment on it in a web editor, then run it remotely or pull it back locally.

---

## Command Changes: `/fork`, `/subtask`, `/code-review`

Week 29 (mid-July 2026) split what used to be a single subagent-launching command in two: **`/fork`** now copies the entire conversation into a new background session with its own row in `claude agents`, while the in-session subagent-launching behavior it previously handled moved to **`/subtask`**. The same week, Claude Code stopped running `/verify` and `/code-review` automatically on its own initiative — both now run only when a user invokes them directly.

---

## Accessibility and Platform Reach

- **Screen reader mode** (Week 29) replaces the visual terminal UI with plain, linear text compatible with VoiceOver and NVDA.
- **Claude Desktop on Linux** entered beta on Ubuntu and Debian (Week 27).
- **Claude in Chrome** reached general availability on all direct Anthropic plans (Week 27).
- **In-app browser on Desktop** (Week 28) lets Claude pull up docs or a live site and interact with it the same way it interacts with local dev-server previews.
- The CLI moved to **native binaries** and gained **mobile push notifications** for long tasks or when Claude needs input (Week 16, April 2026).

---

## Stability and Security

Week 28–29 shipped a broad stability and safety update: tighter permission checks, safer Bash and PowerShell handling, improved background-session cleanup, stronger telemetry, and better remote/plugin reliability. A session-wide cap on WebSearch calls (default 200, tunable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION`) was also added to stop runaway search loops.

---

## Why This Matters

The throughline across these releases is a move away from a single foreground session gated by manual approval, toward multiple concurrent, partly-autonomous agents that a user supervises rather than drives turn-by-turn. Auto mode reduces prompt fatigue; Agent View gives a control-room view across sessions; background subagents and dynamic workflows (see [Claude Model History](claude-model-history) for the Opus 4.8 release that introduced them) let one user's intent fan out into many concurrent workers.
